walkthrough:
Integrate the derivative with respect to $x$ using the power rule:
$$y = \int \left(3x^{1/2} - 3x^{-1/2}\right) dx = 3 \times \frac{x^{3/2}}{3/2} - 3 \times \frac{x^{1/2}}{1/2} + c = 2x^{3/2} - 6x^{1/2} + c$$

Substitute the known coordinates $(4, 7)$ into the integrated expression to find $c$:
$$7 = 2(4^{3/2}) - 6(4^{1/2}) + c = 2(8) - 6(2) + c = 16 - 12 + c = 4 + c$$
$$c = 7 - 4 = 3$$

State the complete equation of the curve:
$$y = 2x^{3/2} - 6x^{1/2} + 3$$
